free_tier.stated: International site (siliconflow.com): a new account is offered USD 1 of credit ('Get started now and enjoy $1 credit to explore our platform!'), and the public international model list prices every model above zero; the rate-limit page says free models carry fixed limits, so any free tag sits in the logged-in console list, which is unverified: behind a sign-up. China site (siliconflow.cn): CNY 14 of free platform credit for a new account, which the vendor equates to 20 million tokens on Qwen1.5-14B: '新用户注册即得 14 元免费额度 (相当于 2 千万 Qwen1.5-14B Tokens)' -- a new account receives CNY 14 of free allowance, equivalent to 20 million Qwen1.5-14B tokens. A second voucher follows real-name verification (amount and validity: unverified), and some small models carry a permanent free tag.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: the free-tagged models consume no credit, so the CNY 14 survives for paid models while a pipeline runs on the free tier; that composition is the only reason the grant stretches.

limits.value: the credit is small and leaves first: CNY 14 buys 20 million tokens on a 14B model, so one long-context job on a frontier model spends it, and the larger CNY 16 voucher sits behind a real-name identity check.

identity_cost.detail: the international sign-in page (account.siliconflow.com) offers Continue with Google and Continue with GitHub, and an email login for accounts that previously used them; it shows no phone field, but its script carries a phone-binding form that is shown when the sign-in callback returns phone=none, and whether the international backend triggers it is unverified: behind a sign-up. The China site (siliconflow.cn) registers by mainland mobile number and its real-name step unlocks the second voucher
